In [[geometry]], the '''pentagonal orthocupolarotunda''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s  ({{math|''J''{{sub|32}}}}).  As the name suggests, it can be constructed by joining a [[pentagonal cupola]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|5}}}}) and a [[pentagonal rotunda]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|6}}}}) along their [[decagon]]al bases, matching the pentagonal faces. A 36-degree rotation of one of the halves before the joining yields a [[pentagonal gyrocupolarotunda]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|33}}}}).

==Formulae==
The following [[formula]]e for [[volume]] and [[surface area]] can be used if all [[faces (geometry)|faces]] are [[regular polygon|regular]], with edge length ''a'':<ref>[[Stephen Wolfram]], "[http://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=Pentagonal+orthocupolarotunda Pentagonal orthocupolarotunda]" from [[Wolfram Alpha]]. Retrieved July 24, 2010.</ref>

:<math>V=\frac{5}{12}\left(11+5\sqrt{5}\right)a^3\approx9.24181...a^3</math>

:<math>A=\left(5+\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{1900+490\sqrt{5}+210\sqrt{75+30\sqrt{5}}}\right)a^2\approx23.5385...a^2</math>
